rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had shown Pharaoh the staff, hand, and other signs; all were perceived by eye and heart, and their extraordinary character demonstrates His power over every possible marvel.
rows.anchor: بالعصا واليد وغيرهما مما تقدم من مقتضى عظمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs and refused to send the Israelites; this concise account is more forceful than the fuller enumeration in al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: وهذا ابلغ من تعديد ما ذكر في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to offer a plausible rebuttal, Pharaoh stirred Egyptian national pride; he recognized Moses’ truth and feared people would follow him, weakening Pharaoh’s own resolve.
rows.anchor: أنه علم حقية ما جاء به موسى وظهوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By calling Moses’ signs magic and claiming Moses would remove them from their land, Pharaoh misled his followers and made their familiar error a barrier to accepting clear proof.
rows.anchor: فخيل إلى أتباعه أن ذلك سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic promise to match Moses’ magic was a deception: Pharaoh knew the signs provoked disbelief that anyone else could produce an equivalent.
rows.anchor: مؤكدا إيذانا بعلمه أن ما أتى به موسى ينكر كل من يراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh proposed an agreed time and place, presenting the contest as fair and binding both sides not to miss it.
rows.anchor: ثم أظهر النصفة والعدل إيثاقا لربط قومه فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suwā means an even, fair place that neither side would find harder to reach than the other.
rows.anchor: أي عدلا بيننا , لا حرج على واحد منا في قصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses chose the Egyptians’ customary festival and gathering place, naming the time here because its regular crowd also implied the venue.
rows.anchor: عيدكم الذي اعدتم الجتماع فيه في المكان الذي اعتدتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A forenoon gathering would expose the contest clearly from the day’s beginning, allow judgment before night, and catch people at their most available.
rows.anchor: ليستقبل النهار من أوله , فيكون أظهر لما يعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The large audience would spread news of the outcome through settlements and among both nomadic and settled people.
rows.anchor: ويكثر المحدث بذلك الأمر العلم في كل بدو وحضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turned from Moses to prepare his plot after turning away from obedience to God; his gathered trickery consisted of the magicians and their devices.
rows.anchor: عن موسى إلى تهيئة ما يريد من الكيد بعد توليه عن الانقياد لأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plot denotes Pharaoh’s deception, contrivance, and trickery, assembled by gathering those who would carry it out.
rows.anchor: أي مكره وحيلته وخداعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egypt then had more magicians than any other land, and Egyptians were especially devoted and skilled in magic.
rows.anchor: وكانوا في ذلك الزمان اشد اعتناء بالسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh arrived for the appointed contest with the magicians he had gathered, his troops, and the people drawn by the festival and spectacle.
rows.anchor: للميعاد الذي وقع القرار عليه بمن حشره من السحرة ةالجنود ومن تبعهم من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God was with Moses and could nullify the magic, He reassured him not to fear any part of their affair.
rows.anchor: وكان المعلوم أم الله معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording answers the expectation that the impressive magic might prevail: Moses alone would be manifestly victorious.
rows.anchor: أي خاصة { الأعلى * } أي الغالب غلبة ظاهرة لا شبهة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff in Moses’ right hand recalls the staff first mentioned when God asked what it was during their initial meeting.
rows.anchor: من هذه العصا التي قلنا لك أول ما شرفناك بالمناجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form suggests forceful, energetic swallowing at a speed scarcely perceived; the omitted tāʾ signals that swiftness.
rows.anchor: بقوة واجتهاد مع سرعة لا تكاد تدرك - بما أشار غليه حذف التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians’ display was the product of extensive training and long practice.
rows.anchor: فعلوه بعد تدرب كبير عليه وممارسة طويلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite singular a magician’s trick belittles the whole company and denies its work substance, whether made by one magician or many; a plural would stress their number instead.
rows.anchor: اي كيد سحري لا حقيقة له ولا ثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magic cannot prevail wherever it goes because it produces only what has no reality.
rows.anchor: فإنه إنما يفعل ما لا حقيقة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff swallowed the display without growing thicker, despite the great quantity of ropes and staffs, so witnesses recognized Moses’ truth and the magicians’ falsehood.
rows.anchor: من غير أن يظهر عليها زيادة في ثخن ولا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians rushed into submission at what they witnessed of God’s power, falling prostrate with extraordinary speed and ease.
rows.anchor: فبادر السحرة منهم إلى الخضوع لأمر الله ساجدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits Moses’ act of throwing the staff and the ensuing swallowing because this sūra emphasizes God’s power to soften hardened hearts.
rows.anchor: وحذف ذكر الإلقاء وما سببه من التلقف لأن مقصود السورة القدرة على تليين القلوب القاسية

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Aṣfahānī marvels that the magicians first cast ropes and staffs in disbelief, then soon cast themselves into prostration in gratitude, a striking contrast between the two acts.
rows.anchor: القوا حبالهم وعصيهم للكفر والجحود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their declaration of faith means that they truly believed and affirmed the truth.
rows.anchor: فما قالوا ؟ فقيل : { قالوا آمنا } أي صدقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun is named before Musa to suit this sūra’s context and foreshadow that the Qur’an will guide people who become humble supporters of the Prophet despite their former pride.
rows.anchor: ولما كان سياق هذه السورة مقتضيا لتقديم هارون عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the Lord points to His favor in raising the brothers above the magicians and above Pharaoh, who claimed lordship but could not help his followers.
rows.anchor: وذكروا اسم الرب إشارة إلى أنه سبحانه أحسن إليهما بإعلاء شأنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians began the day as sorcerers and ended it as righteous witnesses, transformed by what they saw.
rows.anchor: فكانوا أول النهار سحرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of names reflects a meaningful progression through the minister and translator to the one who sent him; it is not an order chosen merely for rhyme.
rows.anchor: ترقيا في درج المعرفة ممن أوصل ذلك إليهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet criticized the disputed kind of contrived sajʿ by comparing it to the rhymed speech of pre-Islamic people or soothsayers.
rows.anchor: وقد عاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك حين قال : ( سجع

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī, as quoted by Abū Ḥayyān, says no Qur’anic wording is advanced or delayed for rhyme, since its inimitability lies in meaning as well as wording.
rows.anchor: قد قال الإمام فخر الدين الرازي كما حكاه عنه الشيخ

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
rows.claim: Al-Bāqillānī reports that his school rejects sajʿ in the Qur’an: in sajʿ meaning follows the rhyme, whereas Qur’anic wording follows the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني في كتاب إعجاز القرآن : ذهب

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿarī also argued in several of his works against classifying Qur’anic passages as sajʿ; apparent rhyme is only an accidental likeness.
rows.anchor: وذكره أبو الحسن الأشعري في غير موضع من كتبه , ثم رد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passage may resemble sajʿ without being it: when meaning is complete independently, rhyme only decorates; Qur’anic wording conveys the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: لأن السجع يتبع المعنى فيه الافظ الذي يؤدي السجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points readers to his discussion at the end of al-Tawba for further argument against explaining Qur’anic word order by rhyme.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في آخر سورة التوبة ما ينفع جدا في هذا المرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means that the magicians believed in God by following or affirming Moses.
rows.anchor: أي بالله { له } أي مصدقين أو متبعين لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By stressing that they acted before his permission, Pharaoh insinuates that he might allow it later, keeping the crowd from following through fear and hope of permission.
rows.anchor: إبهاما بأنه سيأذن فيه ليقف الناس عن المبادرة إلى الاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh invents a prior conspiracy in which Moses was their magic teacher and leader, to stop his followers from accepting the manifest truth.
rows.anchor: فلم تتبعوه لظهور الحق , بل لإرادتكم شيئا من المكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crosswise punishment means cutting one hand and the opposite foot, distributed limb by limb.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التوزيع { وأرجلكم } أي من كل يدا ورجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying they would be crucified in the trunks depicts them as firmly enclosed there, intensifying the horror and deterring others.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الاستعلاء بالظرف إشارة إلى تمكينهم من المصلوب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh challenges whether his punishment or the Lord of Moses’ punishment is harsher and longer-lasting; Moses had warned that punishment befalls whoever denies and turns away.
rows.anchor: أينا عذابه اشد وأطول زمانا

words: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُ خُوَارٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun for them refers to those who drank from the calf and worshipped it.
rows.anchor: فأخرج لهم } أي لمن شربه وعبده

rows.speaker: من جعل هذا كلام من لا يعبد العجل
rows.claim: On one view, the shift to third person shows that the speaker of this statement did not worship the calf.
rows.anchor: يؤيد قول من جعل هذا كلام من لا يعبد العجل

rows.speaker: من جعله من كلام العابدين
rows.claim: On the alternative view that calf-worshippers spoke, their third-person wording signals disavowal and disgust toward it.
rows.anchor: عند من جعله من كلام العابدين أنهم دلوا بذلك على البراءة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Body precedes lowing to clarify that the calf only resembled a living calf in form and was not alive.
rows.anchor: وقدم قوله : { جسدا } لنعرف أن عجليته صورة لا معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samiri declared the calf to be the Israelites’ and Moses’ god, and the first people quickly caught up in the sedition followed him.
rows.anchor: أن السامري قال فتابعه عليه من أسرع في الفتنة أول ما رآه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading is that Moses forgot where the calf was after leaving to search elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فذهب يطلبه في مكان غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Samiri meant that Moses forgot to mention the calf to the people.
rows.anchor: أو نسي أن يذكره لكم

words: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks why they cannot see that the calf neither answers them nor can be a mute deity.
rows.anchor: أي أنه { لا يرجع إليهم قولا } والإله لا يكون أبكم

words: وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf controls neither harm nor benefit; unlike Pharaoh, it gives them no reason to fear retaliation or hope for favor.
rows.anchor: فيخافوه كما يخافون فرعون فيقولوا ذلك خوفا

words: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَارُونُ مِن قَبْلُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun had warned the people about the calf before Moses returned, though the minority who did not worship it could not restrain the majority.
rows.anchor: أي مع أن من لم يعبده لم يملكوا رد من عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun identifies the calf’s extraordinary appearance as a test of whether the Israelites’ faith was sincere and steadfast.
rows.anchor: وقع اختباركم فاختبرتم في صحة إيمانكم وصدقكم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy and favor encompass obedient and sinful people alike, before the calf appeared and afterward; His mercy also leaves repentance open.
rows.anchor: وحده الذي فضله عام ونعمة شاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun urges them to return to God, remain humbly devoted, and obey him so they avoid harm and receive divine good.
rows.anchor: بغية جهدكم في الرجوع إليه { وأطيعوا أمري }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites answer rudely and stubbornly that they will keep assembled around the calf, even if they must fight, until Moses returns.
rows.anchor: بفظاظة وجمود : { لن نبرح عليه } أي على هذا العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses rebukes Harun for not following his practice of restraining wrongdoers, willingly or by force, once he saw them stray.
rows.anchor: من اتباعي في سيرتي فيهم من الخذ على يد الظالم طوعا أو كرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added negative particle intensifies the question: it affirms that Harun should have followed Moses and denies the contrary.
rows.anchor: كان نافيا لضد مضمونه فيفيد إثباتا للمضون ونفيا لضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses treats Harun’s failure to follow him as disobedience and seizes his beard and head in anger for God’s sake.
rows.anchor: وأخذ بلحيته وبرأسه يجره إليه غضبا لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun appeals to their shared mother to soften Moses, although they were full brothers, because a mother is more tender and shares her child’s pain.
rows.anchor: فذكره بها خاصة وإن كان شقيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun’s head means the hair of his head.
rows.anchor: تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي } أي بشعره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun feared that forceful confrontation would be fruitless with few weak supporters and would divide Israel through deaths and kin retaliation.
rows.anchor: بفعلك هذا الذي لم يجد شيئا لقلة من كان معك وضعفكم عن ردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun understood Moses’ instruction to make things right and avoid the corruptors, but not as an order to fight the dissenters even with the sword.
rows.anchor: ولم تقل وارددهم ولو أدى الأمر إلى السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares Harun’s restraint under weak support to Muhammad’s instruction to use pardon, patience, and gentle resistance when allies were few.
rows.anchor: كما كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمورا بالصفح والحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links prayer to the statement that prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing; he omits zakat here because the preceding verse already discourages worldly attachment.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر الزكاة لدخولها في التزهيد بالآية التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The iftiʿāl form of persevere conveys effort: devote yourself to prayer even when it occupies time that could go to livelihood.
rows.anchor: بصيغة الافتعال { عليها } أي على فعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not require the Prophet to earn provision for himself or others; divine majesty means He supplies what would otherwise distract him.
rows.anchor: أي نكلفك طلبه لنفسك ولا لغيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the worry about where provision will come from: He provides for the Prophet and his family from His boundless dominion, including through unexpected means.
rows.anchor: بنون العظمة { نرزقك } لك ولهم ما قدرناه لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not exhaust themselves chasing provision: neither diligence nor neglect can alter the amount allotted to each person from eternity.
rows.anchor: فإن كلا من الجاد فيه والمتهاون به لا يناله أكثر مما قسمناه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who trust God and turn to Him live with contentment and ease; those who turn away and rely on their own effort remain in toil and distress, while the final good outcome belongs to the pious.
rows.anchor: فالمتقي لله المقبل على ذكره واثق بوعده انع راض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No concern about provision rivals prayer in importance.
rows.anchor: ولا معولة على الرزق وغيره توازي الصلاة

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa reports that when something troubled him, the Prophet resorted to prayer; Ahmad transmits the report and al-Baghawī cites it without a full chain at the end of al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: فزع إلى الصلاة - أخرجه أحمد عن حذيفة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām reports that when hardship came to the Prophet’s household, he ordered them to pray and recited this verse; al-Ṭabarānī says it is known only by this chain and Maʿmar alone transmitted it.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سلام رضي الله عنه قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ثابت
rows.claim: Thābit reports that when the Messenger faced hardship, he called his family to pray; Thābit adds that prophets resorted to prayer when an affair distressed them.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت قال : كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصابته خصاصة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports a divine saying promising inner richness and relief from poverty to one who devotes himself to worship, and preoccupation and unmet poverty otherwise; al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening names God as wise and just with complete power and command, Allah as the unrivaled King, the All-Merciful as giving all creation the mercy of existence, and the Merciful as saving whom He wills in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الحكيم العدل الذي تمت قدرته وعم أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: TaHa ends warning that people will learn who is wretched and who is blessed; Anbiya opens with the clearest realization of that warning, the Day of Reckoning when the veil is fully lifted and knowledge becomes direct sight.
rows.anchor: لما ختمت طه بإنذارهم بأنهم سيعلمون الشقي والسعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection; ḥisāb also means enumerating something and requiting it with good or evil.
rows.anchor: والحساب : إحصاء الشيء والمجازاة عليه بخير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The iftiʿāl form intensifies the nearness because no later community remains whose turn must first arrive.
rows.anchor: بصيغة الافتعال غلى مزيد القرب لأنه لا أمة بعد هذه ينتظر أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delaying the subject their account heightens suspense by letting the listener imagine what is approaching.
rows.anchor: وأخر الفاعل تهويلا لتذهب النفس في تعيينه كل مذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, account can mean recompense, making the verse a threat of events such as Badr and the Conquest, with people referring to Quraysh or all Arabs.
rows.anchor: ويصح أن يراد بالحساب الجزاء , فيكون ذلك تهديدا بيوم بدر والفتح ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the primary reading, people means everyone generally, including the addressees and others.
rows.anchor: أي عامة أنتم وغيركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word nās is associated with naws, restlessness that prevents people from remaining secure and steady; only very few are saved from this deficiency.
rows.anchor: من أجل ما في جبلاتهم من النوس , وهو الاضطراب الموجب لعدم الثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their heedlessness is exposed when they are raised, or when events kill them and leave survivors humbled, so that they recognize truth and falsehood.
rows.anchor: لأنهم إذا نشروا علموت , وإذا أبادتهم الوقائع علموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from God’s warnings causes their heedlessness; the closing confession that they were wrongdoers will confirm this, though reason already requires requital of good and evil.
rows.anchor: أحاطت بهم الغفلة بسبب إعراضهم عما يأتيهم منا , وسيأتي ما يؤيد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the near account to the preceding warning not to covet worldly goods: their abundance is a trial and people will answer for every blessing, so the reckoning is near.
rows.anchor: أي لا تمدن عينيك إلى ذلك فإني جعلته فتنة لمن ناله بغير حق

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The earlier warning about a contentious people and destruction of past generations called for fuller consolation and explanation, which this sūra supplies.
rows.anchor: وهم شديدو الخصومة في الباطل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: TaHa consoles the Prophet with the assurance that the Qur’an was not sent to make him suffer, then with Moses’ struggle against Pharaoh, his ruin, and the inheritance of his land by God’s servants.
rows.anchor: وتأنيسه بقصة موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The story of Adam and his struggle with Iblis also comforts Muhammad: it shows that hardship from an adversary is God’s established way with His servants.
rows.anchor: ثم اتبعت بقصة آدم عليه السلام ليرى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Anbiya continues this consolation by showing the approaching Judgment and good outcome of striving for God, whose reward makes even greater hardship desirable.
rows.anchor: فبين اقتراب الحساب ووقوع يوم الفصل المحمود فيه ثمرة ما كوبد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: After its consolation, the sūra presents admonitions, proofs, and signs, and recalls God’s established practice of destroying earlier communities that did not believe.
rows.anchor: وأعلم أنه سبحانه قد سبقت سنته بإهلاك من لم يكن منه الإيمان

none: The segment contains only quoted verse fragments and references, without explanatory commentary.
